RESPONDENT NO.2 HEREIN.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The defacto complainant has filed this petition under Section 439(2) of Cr.PC with a prayer to set aside the order dated 29.09.2023 passed by the Court of IV Addl. District & Sessions Judge, D.K.,
Mangaluru, in Crl. Misc. No.802/2023, wherein anticipatory bail was granted to respondent no.2 herein in Crime No.118/2023 registered by Mangaluru East Police Station, D.K., Mangaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 354, 504, 34 IPC and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2008.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.118/2023 was registered by Mangaluru East Police Station, D.K., Mangaluru,
against respondent no.2 herein and another for the aforesaid offences.

entities.text: Mangaluru East Police Station, D.K., Mangaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Complainant - Sweety Somashekhar had filed a typed complaint dated 04.09.2023 before the Station House Officer of Mangaluru East NC: 2023:KHC:46058 Police Station, D.K., Mangaluru, wherein it is alleged that she was acquainted with respondent no.2 herein who was running a Skin Clinic known as Cosmedics at Kadri in Mangaluru.

She allegedly introduced accused no.2 to the complainant and they together started a company known as THA Transformation Pvt. Ltd., and the complainant was also inducted as a Director to the said company and she allegedly had invested a sum of Rs.15 lakhs in the said company and the accused had assured that they will be paying interest at 18% per annum on the said investment.
Subsequently, the complainant had retired as the Director of the company, but when she requested the accused persons to return the amount invested by her, they allegedly had misbehaved with her.
Accused no.2 had forwarded a whatsapp message which was indecent and he also tried to outrage her modesty.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, respondent no.2 who was Sweety Hassana Somashekar vs The State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45249936/
2 arrayed as accused no.1 in Crime No.118/2023 had filed Crl. Misc. No.802/2023 before the Court of IV Addl. District & Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangaluru, which was allowed on 29.09.2023.

sentences.text: Challenging the said order, the defacto complainant has approached this Court.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the Sessions Court was not justified in allowing the bail application considering the nature of allegation made against the accused persons.
He submits that the Trial Court has observed that the dispute between the parties is civil in nature and the same would seriously affect the trial of the case.
5. Per contra, learned Counsel for respondent no.2 has opposed the petition.

6. From a perusal of the material available on record, it is seen that the defacto complainant was the Director of the company known as THA Transformation Pvt. Ltd., and she allegedly had invested Rs.15 lakhs in the said company.
Accused nos.1 & 2 were also the Directors of the said company.
The defacto complainant allegedly had resigned from the company as Director and thereafter had demanded repayment of the amount allegedly invested by her.

According to the complainant,
accused no.2 had forwarded some whatsapp message which was obscene and he also had allegedly tried to outrage her modesty.
Respondent no.2 herein who is arrayed as accused no.1 in the FIR is a lady aged about 26 years.
The NC: 2023:KHC:46058 maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for a period of seven years.

Considering the nature of allegations, the learned Sessions Judge has granted anticipatory bail to respondent no.2.
7.
From a perusal of the said order, it is seen that cogent reasons have been assigned by the learned Sessions Judge for granting anticipatory bail and no fault can be found in the same.
The petitioner has not made out any exceptional and supervening circumstances for canceling the said order under which anticipatory bail has been granted to respondent no.2.
Under the circumstances, I am not inclined to interfere with the said order.

8. However, it is made clear that any observation made by the learned Sessions Judge with regard to the nature of dispute between the parties while disposing of Crl. Misc. No.802/2023 vide order dated 29.09.2023 shall not have any bearing on the merits of the case and the Trial Court without being influenced by any such observation, shall dispose of the case strictly on its merits.
NC: 2023:KHC:46058 9.
With the above observation, this petition is disposed of.
